It has been nearly a year since counties across WNC received nearly $10 million in state grant funding to boost rural broadband connectivity. With public education in North Carolina shifting to at-home distance learning amid the COVID-19 outbreak and businesses across the state being ordered to allow employees to work from home wherever possible, the need for broadband is greater than ever.
In May 2019, North Carolina issued the Growing Rural Economies with Access to Technology (GREAT) grant. The matching grants went to “Internet service providers and electric membership cooperatives that compete for funding to lower financial barriers that prevent high speed internet service expansion in Tier 1 – which is identified as economically distressed counties,” according to Gov. Roy Cooper and the NC Department of Information Technology.
Launched by the N.C. General Assembly in 2018, the program subsidizes Internet providers and electric cooperatives who are working with unserved and underserved rural communities across the state.
“Access to reliable, high-speed internet service is critical for businesses to grow, students to learn, and communities to thrive,” Cooper said in announcing the funding. “These grants will help connect thousands of homes and businesses with opportunities across the state and around the world.”
The grants went to assist 14 companies – including Morris Broadband which serves Macon County – improve broadband for some 10,000 households plus almost 600 businesses and community institutions.
“The construction process began the last quarter of 2019,” said Morris Broadband General Manager Tony Carter. “That involved engineering design, pole permits and pole replacements and other make-ready preparations. Those have all been filed and are just awaiting a few more responses and replacements until we can begin construction.”
Carter said the company is now switching its focus to the physical construction of the expansion project, which will begin within the next few weeks.
“We anticipate the physical, visible construction to begin sometime in April,” said Carter. “All expansions we have on our plate have always been considered an urgency as all of them involve under-served areas and will continue to be a top priority for us.”
The Morris expansion will ideally provide internet access to 226 homes within Macon County. The project was estimated to cost $667,000 which included $433,550 in state grant money along with a $233,450 investment from Morris.
Morris Broadband currently provides just under 3,500 residences in Macon County with internet services. The 226 homes are located in various outlying areas of the county.

Only three months after late activist Edith Windsor’s 2013 victory for gay rights at the Supreme Court, which led to the national legalization of same-sex marriage, The New York Times ran an article questioning the resolve of queer theatres to evolve with the times.
“At a time of rapid change in the gay-rights movement, from marriage to the military, the purpose of a strictly gay theatre company isn’t the same as it was 10 years ago,” remarked Times contributor Erik Piepenburg. The writer observed a general decline in interest for LGBTQ topics and a subsequent drop at gay-specific companies in both revenues and taste. The logical result? Queer theatre companies were opting for lighter, campier fare, Piepenburg wrote, to keep their audiences happy.
Underlying this high-profile conclusion is the anxiety that queer theatre cannot survive the shifting tides of public opinion. Without antipathy, is there just apathy? Without something to fight against, does the once edgy avant-garde of queer theatre disappear?
Elsewhere, critics have eviscerated a handful of once-classic gay works as shallow, dated excursions. Reflecting on the autumn 2016 season, The New Yorker’s Hilton Als wrote a particularly brutal assessment of William Finn and James Lapine’s Broadway revival of Falsettos.

If you're struggling on what to have for dinner Tuesday night, why not make it a pizza and help with the eradication of polio?
The Rotary Club of LaSalle Centennial is teaming up with local pizza shops for the annual Pizza for Polio fundraiser.
All day Tuesday, more than a dozen pizzerias across Windsor-Essex will be donating a portion of their proceeds to Rotary International's Global Polio Eradication Initiative.
Coordinator Mary Lou Amlin says it's as easy as ordering a pizza.
"That money will go to help eradicate polio worldwide which is something that Rotary has been working on since 1988. At this time, we only have two countries left in the world that have any polio in them. Those are Afghanistan and Pakistan."
She says the world is nearly polio free.
"As Rotarians we say we're 99% there trying to eradicate polio. So this is another push, it's a worldwide Rotarian effort to gain funds in order to eradicate polio."
Amlin says it's beneficial for both the pizza shops and Rotary.
"We're thrilled that they can partner with us and want to support us and support the eradication of polio. We're just thrilled about that. This year too, with COVID, it's really beneficial for them. It's an opportunity to get them more sales. So it really is a win/win."

Our view of the soft sciences grows dimmer by the day, but it’s good to know there are at least a few people involved with the discipline who haven’t completely lost their minds. While most sociologists were quick to jump on the woke bandwagon (to the extent they weren’t responsible for building that wagon in the first place), one professor at the University of Illinois is warning that today’s tendency to smear everything and everyone as “racist” is having the opposite of its intended effect.
In an article for Persuasion, Professor Ilana Redstone said that using that term to describe everything that violates your political philosophy has robbed it of any meaning whatsoever.
“The charge of racism can be reputation-destroying and have long-term psychological effects,” Redstone wrote. “Yet its excessive application dilutes that power—for example, applying the word ‘racist’ to both Dylann Roof, the white supremacist who murdered nine black worshippers at a South Carolina church in 2015, and a local-business promotion in Seattle involving decorative monkeys. The antiracist strategy is not only weakening its own best weapon, it’s backfiring.”
Redstone went on to explain that one can support racial equality without buying into the woke, “antiracist” propaganda.
“The argument of antiracist activists is that, if you stand against their methods, you oppose their ends, no matter how much you insist otherwise. Unsurprisingly, this has narrowed the spectrum of acceptable views on sensitive topics,” she wrote. For example, opposition to affirmative action and support for increased border restrictions are two positions labeled racist under the expanded definition. Racial hostility is a possible motivation for those positions. After all, affirmative action was intended to benefit members of under-represented minorities; and much of the immigration to the West in the 21st century involves non-white migrants.
“But one might have non-racist motives for such views, including concerns over whether affirmative action is the best way to help the targeted groups,” she continued.

The Buccaneers didn’t play in Week 13. Which means that there was no reason for Buccaneers coach Bruce Arians to directly criticize (a/k/a be honest) or to passive-aggressively snipe at quarterback Tom Brady. Instead, Arians heaped praise on Brady.
“It’s been fantastic,” Arians told reporters when asked about working with Brady. “From day one, getting him here [and] watching him prepare and help young players get better. He’s a joy to coach and he’s a fantastic competitor. I love that about him. He’s been there and done it and he’s helped so many of our guys who haven’t [been there] believe that they can. That’s a huge part of it and I couldn’t ask any more out of him.”
Arians also praised Brady’s overall ability to show up and work every day, despite being 43.
“I don’t see any drop at all,” Arians said. “I’ve had some veteran guys that needed Wednesdays off and he’s not one of those guys. He’s amazing that way and how he takes care of himself. He’s helped a lot of young players learn about taking care of themselves also.”
Brady’s leadership and experience likewise was praised.
“There’s no doubt about it,” Arians said. “I’ve been very, very fortunate with some of the best quarterbacks that all have that. Every single one I’ve probably ever coached have had that ability. Peyton [Manning], Ben [Roethlisberger], Andrew Luck as a rookie was amazing. Tom [Brady], Timmy Couch, Kelly Holcomb — every one of those guys that were successful. When they got in the huddle, they had the ability to make everybody believe that this is the best play that’s going to be called and run. Then, walk off, work with guys, take them to the side, work with them and bring them along. All those great ones do it.”
Arians also didn’t take the bait when asked whether he’s frustrated with the offense’s inability to properly execute the scripted plays to start the game.

PYONGYANG, North Korea (AP) -- International Olympic Committee President Thomas Bach has met with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Pyongyang.
Bach told an Associated Press Television crew the two had a 30-minute formal meeting followed by 45 minutes of casual talking while watching a football match Friday afternoon at Pyongyang's huge May Day Stadium. He said Kim supports a plan to have North Korean athletes compete in the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics and the 2022 Beijing Winter Games.
Bach arrived in Pyongyang on Thursday to discuss development of sports in North Korea and the preparation of its athletes to qualify and participate in upcoming Olympics. He is the first foreign official to meet Kim since the North Korean leader returned from a summit in Beijing with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

A standing COVID-19 vaccine clinic at La Palmera and a program to vaccinate homeless people are in the works, Corpus Christi and Nueces County officials said Thursday.
The La Palmera clinic will launch Tuesday and will be open Monday through Sunday during regular mall hours, public health director Annette Rodriguez said during the city and county’s weekly COVID-19 briefing.
People can pre-register or register on site, Rodriguez said. Officials hope to have at least 100 doses available every day.
To pre-register, visit cctexas.com/vaccineregistration or call 361-561-1101.
The clinic will be in the former Charming Charlie location near Grimaldi’s, Rodriguez said.
The mall is “a place that most of us might go anyway,” Nueces County Judge Barbara Canales said. “Whether you’re shopping or dining or getting your free, life-saving COVID-19 vaccine shot, it sounds like it’s a good day to be at La Palmera.
“La Palmera will be part of the many tools we have to fight back against this horrible disease.”
Homeless population
With shipments of Johnson and Johnson on the way, the city is working with providers of homeless services to identify the best way to reach that population, city spokeswoman Christian Cabazos said.
Unlike the two-dose vaccines by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, the Johnson and Johnson vaccine requires only one dose. Experts say that makes it an ideal option for hard-to-reach populations.
“Your city and your health district are working to ensure that all populations have access to the vaccine,” Cabazos said.
Save Our Seniors
Registration for the Save Our Seniors vaccination program will open at noon Friday.

JOHANNESBURG, May 26 (Reuters) - Gold miner AngloGold Ashanti ANGJ.J said on Wednesday the ramp-up of production at its Obuasi mine in Ghana would be delayed, with operations remaining suspended after a miner went missing last week following a collapse of ground.
The firm said the search for the worker were ongoing. Obuasi produced 34,000 ounces between April and the suspension of underground mining activities on May 18.

Saudi king hosts Abbas after Palestinian accord
RIYADH: Palestinian President Mahmud Abbas held talks with Saudi King Salman on Tuesday on his first visit to the kingdom since last month´s landmark reconciliation accord between rival factions Hamas and Fatah.
"During the session, the (two leaders) reviewed the latest developments in the Palestinian arena," state-run Saudi Press Agency said in a brief statement.
Under an Egyptian-brokered deal signed between Abbas´s Fatah and the Islamist Hamas movement on October 12, the Palestinian Authority is due to resume full control of the Gaza Strip by December 1.
Abbas´s visit to Riyadh comes after Hamas handed over control of the Gaza Strip´s borders with Egypt and Israel to the Palestinian Authority last week, in the first key test of the accord.

The digital landscape has transformed drastically since the era of mainframes. Your company, like many others, has ridden each wave of technological advancement, from minis and microcomputers to the PC revolution, the dot-com boom with Sparcs, and the rise of databases like DB2, Oracle, and SQL Server. You embraced MPP, explored data cubes, and transitioned data to the intranet and internet.  VMware promised to control server sprawl, yet VM sprawl emerged. SharePoint became a fixture, and the allure of SaaS led you from Siebel to Salesforce.

Now, you're drowning in data. Your mainframe is a fragile relic, your SAN a costly black box offering little insight due to rampant VM and application sprawl.  Millennials advocate for "webscale" solutions like MongoDB, while Hadoop vendors promise magical insights from data lakes, introducing yet another storage technology to manage.

Enough is enough. This year, regain control of your data.  Here are 12 resolutions to guide your data strategy:

1. **Catalog Your Data:**  Knowing what data you possess is the first step. A comprehensive data mapping system is helpful, but the crucial element is a dedicated effort to locate and document all your data assets.

2. **Map Data Use:** Understand how your data is used by applications and its flow within the organization. Tracking data lineage and dependency, whether through software or manual effort, is vital.  Identify why data is kept, who uses it, and for what purpose. Define the data, its source system, and its usage.

3. **Understand Data Creation:**  Just as NASA’s reliance on incomplete data led to critical errors, understanding your data's origins is crucial. How are numbers derived?  This is an ongoing process, as new data sources constantly emerge, but it's essential for preventing avoidable disasters.

4. **Understand Data Flow:**  Mapping your organization’s data circulatory system—a comprehensive data flow diagram—is essential. This reveals inefficiencies ("black holes" and "miracles"), redundancies, and opportunities for optimization.  It also highlights where similar processes differ solely by technology stack, allowing for standardization.

5. **Automate Manual Processes:** Manual data manipulation in spreadsheets introduces latency and errors. By mapping your data flow, you can identify these manual processes and automate them, improving efficiency and accuracy.

6. **Embrace Machine Learning:**  Machine learning isn't magic, but it can automate pattern recognition and analysis. Identify at least one business process where machine learning can provide a demonstrable advantage. This is a practical step towards leveraging the power of data.

7. **Prioritize Natural Language and Voice Search:**  The future of data interaction is natural language and voice.  Making your data accessible through these modalities is no longer a luxury but a necessity to cater to evolving user expectations.

8. **Embrace Web Accessibility:**  Shift away from cumbersome desktop software.  Web-based applications offer greater flexibility, easier maintenance, and accessibility from anywhere.

9. **Prioritize Mobile Accessibility:**  Desktop computing is declining.  Ensure your data and applications are accessible on mobile devices to support the increasingly mobile workforce.

10. **Ensure High Availability and Distributability:**  Resilience is key.  Modern distributed databases designed for the cloud offer better uptime, scalability, and more affordable disaster recovery than traditional solutions.

11. **Consolidate Systems:** Simplify your IT infrastructure by consolidating redundant systems. This reduces complexity, maintenance costs, and improves overall efficiency.  While the business case may be challenging, the long-term benefits are significant.

12. **Visualize Data:**  Charts and visualizations make data more accessible and understandable.  Leverage visualization tools to communicate insights effectively.


By adopting these resolutions, you can transform IT from a cost center to a strategic asset, building a data-driven future for your organization.

Hoosier Racing Tire SCCA Super Tour competition got rolling Saturday on a weekend hosted by Cal Club at Buttonwillow Raceway Park in California. The day opened with a second round of qualifying followed by 25-minute timed races on the 2.95-mile circuit being run counterclockwise this year.

2020 GT-3 Challenge Begins: This year’s GT-3 Challenge presented by MPI opened this weekend as part of the Buttonwillow Super Tour event, and the series’ first race took place Saturday in dry conditions. Michael Lewis, in the No. 32 Goodyear Mazda RX-7, started on pole and led every lap on his way to victory. Behind him, however, things got interesting: Taz Harvey’s Mazda RX-7 held down second for most of the race. But Jose Rodriguez, also in a Mazda RX-7, hounded Harvey almost the entire time, grabbing second with only a couple of laps to go. Harvey brought his car home in third to round out the podium.

The GT-3 Challenge is a series aimed at boosting participation in the GT-3 class and supported by Mazda, Max Papis Innovations, Penske Racing Shocks, AiM Sports, and Hoosier Racing Tire, with new partners Goodyear Tire, Carbotech Performance Brakes, and Bell Racing Helmets jumping aboard this year. There are five scheduled GT-3 Challenge rounds in 2020, the others taking place at Super Tour events at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta and Watkins Glen International, as well as Road America in July, and finally SCCA’s National Championship Runoffs in October.

Then Came the Rain: Saturday’s second race group consisted of fast, open-cockpit formula and prototype cars. And just as they pulled off grid for their pace lap, a light rain began to fall on the circuit. On slick tires, these cars don’t take kindly to wet surfaces. And on the opening lap in Turn 1, they showed it as a bunch of cars got squirrely, sliding sideways and collecting other cars. Those who emerged victorious after 25 minutes had one heck of a story to tell.

“There was a big melee at the exit of Turn 1. I’m not sure who was even involved in it, but cars were going everywhere,” said Bill Weaver, who drove his No. 67 James G. Parker Insurance Associates Star Formula Mazda to victory in the Formula X class. “I hit somebody. The front of my car launched up into the air, probably about three feet into the air. But it came down and the wheels were still on, so I just kept driving it. No front wing and a wet track is exciting to say the least. But we got it done, finished the race and had a great time.”

Sweep Ceased: Over the last two years, Mike Miserendino has claimed all four Hoosier Super Tour Spec Racer Ford Gen3 races at Buttonwillow Raceway Park. On Saturday, Miserendino looked set to do it again as he came to the white flag with the lead over TJ Acker. But, on the back half of the last lap, the top-two drivers encountered traffic and Acker, driving the No. 62 MBI Racing / Cindescency racecar, ended up crossing the finish line first.

“We had a couple of lapped cars to deal with, and I thought that would give Mike the tow to keep out in front of me,” said Acker, who also took a win Saturday in Formula Enterprises 2 driving the No. 62 Bulldog Motorsports Formula Enterprises/Mazda car. “But I got a good run and I think we were three-wide coming off the back straight. I had the inside and had the position getting up the hill … and got the lead.”

Doubles on the Day: Winning one Hoosier Super Tour event is pretty special. Winning two Super Tour races on the same day, that’s even more special. Besides Acker, two other drivers accomplished that feat on Saturday. One was Christopher Qualls, who drove his Ford Mustang to victory in both Touring 2 and American Sedan. Michael Lewis achieved the same by driving his No. 12 Goodyear Jaguar XKR to victory in GT-1 after claiming the GT-3 win earlier in the day.

Powers On: Leading Spec Miata to the start line Saturday was Dakota Dickerson, a former F4 U.S. and the reigning F3 Americas champion. But early on up front it was Steven Powers, Justin Casey, Tristan Littlehale and Nick Leverone. Several of those drivers took a turn at the front or applied copious amounts of pressure to whomever was leading. On the last lap, Leverone made an amazing run down the backstretch and tried to challenge Powers, who was leading.

Sebastian Vettel has led calls for an investigation into the apparent tyre failures suffered by Lance Stroll and Max Verstappen during the Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Both drivers suffered heavy high-speed crashes after their left-rear tyres seemed to give way, prompting concern for driver safety on the track.

On Lap 30, Stroll was pitched into the wall on the drivers’ left as he rounded Turn 19—a kink in the long front straight. The Canadian was still running the hard compound Pirelli tyres on which he’d started the race at the time of the incident. Later, Verstappen crashed out only metres up the road with a seemingly identical problem, having pitted on Lap 12 to swap his soft tyres for a set of the hard compound rubber and crashing out 32 laps later.

Indeed, it prompted Red Bull’s sporting director Jonathan Wheatley to radio FIA race director Michael Masi, advising that there was no warning prior to Verstappen’s failure. He effectively recommended the race be red-flagged on safety grounds. Speeds down the more than two-kilometre front straight in Baku easily exceed 300kmh, making it one of the fastest sections of track all season. As a street circuit, it is hemmed in by walls, offering little opportunity for the driver to react and save the car before careering into a concrete barrier.

“I saw that he lost the car very late in the straight,” Vettel said of his Aston Martin team-mate Stroll’s crash. “I thought maybe first he clipped the wall outside of 19. But then I looked the next lap, and there was not a scratch. That would have been very unusual, but I couldn’t explain why he would crash so late in the straight.

In a shocking and gruesome incident, a 17-year-old boy, identified as Swethan, was brutally hacked to death by a group of men in Tamil Nadu's Cuddalore district. The attackers decapitated the teenager, wrapped his severed head in a gunny bag, and later threw it at the entrance of a police station. The headless body was found dumped in a lake approximately three kilometers away from the station.

Chilling CCTV footage captured two bikers arriving at the police station, flinging the severed head at the entrance, and speeding away. According to the police, the murder was carried out by a gang involved in chain-snatching and bike theft in the region. Investigators suspect the incident is linked to ongoing gang wars in the area.

A former police detective is behind bars after stealing thousands of pounds in cash seized from passengers at Heathrow Airport. Michael Harrington, 46, from Staines, worked at the airport as a Detective Sergeant with the Metropolitan Police, tasked with carrying out financial investigations and seizing unauthorised cash from those travelling in and out of the country. During his five years in the role, between July 2009 and July 2015, it is estimated that he stole between £75,000 and £83,000 from 16 victims, according to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

In some instances, Harrington seized cash from victims and then falsely recorded that it had been given back after it was found to be lawful money. In others, he recorded the amounts seized to be less than they actually were, pocketing whole sums in the process. The disgraced former financial investigator was jailed for four-and-a-half years for 16 counts of theft at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday (February 28).

Riaz Jakhura, from the CPS London’s Complex Casework unit, said: "Harrington took advantage of a number of passengers, including foreign nationals making their way through Heathrow Airport. He abused his position as a financial investigator for the police, contributing to significant stress and financial hardship for some of his victims. The overwhelming evidence against Harrington meant that he had no choice but to admit his crimes."

Two victims suffered financial loss when attending weddings abroad without the legitimate money they had planned to take with them. On one occasion, Harrington denied a victim the opportunity to have an interpreter present when confiscating legitimate money. He was caught when victims started to contact police about getting back the money seized, leading the police to Harrington. Harrington, who had been suspended from the Met Police pending the completion of the court case, admitted the thefts in October last year.

He had previously failed to turn up to an earlier sentence hearing, prompting a warrant for his arrest.

Harris Grill, a well-known Pittsburgh eatery with locations in Downtown and Shadyside, has announced that it is permanently closing its Fourth Avenue location in Downtown Pittsburgh. The last day of service at this location will be Thursday, December 30.

In a press release, the Harris Grill team cited struggles to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic as the reason behind the closure. "The Harris Grill 4th Avenue has struggled to remain open since the Coronavirus pandemic descended in March of 2020," the release stated. "With the loss of the downtown business office population and cancellation of cultural trust activities, sales have been down 75%." While some business has returned, the restaurant noted that "there is simply not enough continuing and regular foot traffic for the number of restaurants currently attempting to operate downtown."

The decision by some Downtown offices to delay or modify their return to in-person work has also impacted Harris Grill's cash flow issues. Furthermore, Allegheny County is still experiencing a high number of COVID-19 daily cases, and officials expect the situation to worsen as the Omicron variant spreads and people travel and socialize for the winter holidays.

The Pittsburgh Steelers held their final practice before Monday’s game against Washington, and three key players were missing.  Starting quarterback Ben Roethlisberger (knee) was held out and listed as questionable, as was starting cornerback Steven Nelson (knee), who is doubtful for Monday.  Placekicker Chris Boswell (hip) was also sidelined and is questionable for the game.

Nelson’s absence is expected, as he suffered a knee injury against Baltimore on Wednesday and underwent an MRI on Thursday.  Boswell’s hip issue, however, is new, as he wasn't on the injury report before Saturday. If Boswell can't play, the Steelers will likely elevate Matthew Wright from the practice squad.  The Steelers signed Wright just five days ago, choosing him over Brandon Wright, a 23-year-old rookie from Georgia State, after a tryout.

At the time, it appeared Wright's signing was a precaution against a COVID-19 emergency, as the Steelers also added a backup long-snapper to the practice squad. But the move may also have been  preemptive, given Boswell’s hip.

Wright, a Central Florida alum, isn't entirely new to the Steelers, although he hasn't kicked in a regular-season NFL game.  He signed with Pittsburgh as an undrafted free agent in 2019 and competed with Boswell for the placekicking job during the preseason, converting five of six field goal attempts.  The Steelers ultimately stuck with Boswell, who rewarded them with a resurgent 2019 season and a stellar 2020 performance (16 of 17 field goals made).

# Neeraj Chopra's Journey to Tokyo Olympics: A Story of Comeback and Resilience

## The Triumphant Return
In a remarkable comeback, Neeraj Chopra threw 87.86m at the ACNW League Meet in Potchefstroom, South Africa, qualifying for the Tokyo Olympics by clearing the 85m mark. This achievement, coming after a 1.5-year hiatus, was particularly significant - the distance exceeded the 86.89m throw that won gold at the 2019 World Championships.

"I feel proud of making a strong comeback. Participating in a competition after 1.5 years and clearing the Olympic mark gives me immense satisfaction," Chopra says.

## The Injury Setback
The road to this comeback wasn't smooth. Following a stellar 2018, where he claimed gold at both Commonwealth Games and Asian Games and set a national record of 88.06 metres, Chopra began experiencing elbow pain in November 2018.

"I started feeling my injury back in November 2018. I continued to train, but was not having too many issues despite the pain. But it aggravated by April," he recalled. The condition worsened until he couldn't even lift a javelin, leading to surgery in May 2019.

## The Rehabilitation Journey
Post-surgery, Chopra underwent an intensive rehabilitation period, first in Mumbai and then at JSW's Inspire Institute of Sport in Bellary. He began with basic activities like cycling, gradually progressing to hand exercises and strength training.

"After surgery, I immediately started cycling, because I was unable to move my hand. Later, I started hand and strengthening exercises and slowly started gaining my strength. I kept myself motivated by setting a target for myself each day to do better than the previous day."

## World Championships Disappointment
Despite qualifying for the World Athletics Championships with an 83.90m throw in September 2018, Chopra had to withdraw due to his recovery. "I had trained really hard for the World Championships. It was constantly on my mind, whenever I was at the training. But injury ki wajah se sab gadbad ho gaya," he explained.

## The Path Forward
With the Olympic qualification secured, Chopra isn't resting on his laurels. He's already back in training, preparing for the Federation Cup and IAAF Diamond League in Doha in April, leading up to the Tokyo Olympics where he could become India's first track-and-field Olympic medalist since 1900.

"My target of qualifying for Tokyo is accomplished. From the next day onwards, I restarted my original training schedule. The preparations have begun for the Tokyo Olympics and for all the competitions that are on the road," he says.

## Mental Resilience
Throughout his recovery, Chopra maintained a positive attitude. "Everyone told me that injuries are a part of an athlete's life'. They told me not to worry too much about time off the track and just focus on my recovery."

"I believed I could qualify for Tokyo because I was having a good time at the training. Everything was working out and bhaari haath chal raha tha. So, I was expecting a good comeback. But the fact that I qualified on my first attempt, it makes me really happy," he concluded.

Korean-American hip-hop artist Jay Park recently reflected on his past negative comments about Korea. On October 1, Netflix released the first episode of the original show 'Paik's Spirit,' featuring Jay Park and fellow hip-hop artist Loco as guests. During a meal, Loco brought up the time when Jay Park faced heavy criticism for his past remarks.

In 2009, comments Jay Park made about Korea in 2005, shortly after he began training at JYP Entertainment, were discovered on his personal social media. Written in English to a friend, they read, "Korea is gay. I hate Koreans. I want to go back." These comments quickly spread online. Just three days later, Jay Park left his group, 2PM, and returned to his hometown of Seattle in the United States.

Reflecting on this period, Jay Park explained, "It wasn't entirely my decision to come to Korea at first. When I was asked to join JYP Entertainment, my mom suggested I should go for our future. My family was struggling financially in Seattle, and she thought I could earn good money there."

He continued, "There were many popular artists at JYP Entertainment, but I didn't know much about JYP or Korea. I went for my family. Life in Korea was very different from what I expected. It was my first time living away from my family and friends, and I had given up everything in Seattle for that. It wasn't easy for me; the cultural differences were challenging. I may have complained to my friends back in the States, and that's where those comments came from."

Jay Park added, "After I started gaining attention as the leader of 2PM, someone dug up those comments from the social media account I no longer used, and it became an issue. People kept saying, 'Jay Park hates Korea and Koreans,' but that can't be true because my parents are Korean, and I'm Korean myself."

He concluded, "Anyway, I was ignorant and thoughtless back then. I was too young, and my words came out wrong. I think I expected everyone to live like I did. I was too selfish.

CAPE TOWN (Reuters) - South African lawmakers elected Cyril Ramaphosa as state president on Wednesday, May 22, 2019, in the first parliamentary sitting since the ruling African National Congress (ANC) secured a majority in the general election earlier this month. Car-buying consumers are at great risk after weather events like Hurricane Harvey and the threat posed by Hurricane Irma. They're at risk that flooded vehicles will eventually flood the market. The late Tom Zimmer, a former National Insurance Crime Bureau investigator and long-time source of mine, demonstrated for me three years ago how states will print salvage titles in the insurance companies' names -- and in a different color. "A regular Tennessee title is going to be green," he demonstrated. "Notice how the (Tennessee salvage title) is blue."

By law, when a flood drowns cars on a retail or auction lot, the lot must total out those vehicles in coordination with its insurance company and brand those cars' titles as salvage titles in the name of the insurance company. It also takes days, even weeks to secure a salvage title on a flooded vehicle. There's the flood itself, then the waiting to get a claims adjuster out to conduct an inspection, then the determination of loss and liability, then the generation of the title. "There's a gap of time between the actual incident and the branding of the title, so basically, you are unprotected at that point until those titles are branded," said Stan Norton, managing partner of City Auto and dealer member of the Tennessee Motor Vehicle Commission.

Bottom line, you should never buy a car without proof of a clean title. Period. If you insist on taking the risk of considering a car that has either a salvage title or no title at all, Zimmer said use your eyes -- and your nose -- to determine if it may be a flooded vehicle. "Are there artificial air fresheners in there that are probably covering up the odor of mold?" he said. He also said look for sand, dirt or silt traces in the upholstery, on the floorboard and around the interior. Chris Basso, public relations director for Carfax vehicle history reports, recommended before purchasing the car, have a reliable mechanic inspect the trunk, engine, and spare tire well for water or debris. Look for condensation in the dashboard, headlights, and taillights -- and look for excess rust on interior metal parts.

Andy Wise walks you through the steps of filing a flooded vehicle claim, as long as you have comprehensive coverage. "You should rely on vehicle history reports, and you should absolutely get those," Norton said.

Additionally, he cited Berlin's growing influence in the internet sector, particularly its focus on the US market, which is Archify's target audience. Bäck also revealed that attending a start-up boot camp in Copenhagen cemented the realization that remaining in Vienna was not a viable option for the company's growth. While the five-person team plans to transition to Berlin, Bäck intends to initially commute between the Austrian and German capitals.

Archify is developing a personal search engine designed to complement Google.  Bäck explained, "Google is great for searching for information you don't yet know." Traffic safety experts have tried various strategies to combat speeding, as speeding-related crashes claim around 12,000 American lives annually. Initially, they attempted flashing signs to alert drivers of their speed, believing that drivers would slow down if they were aware of their speed. When this method proved ineffective, they deployed law enforcement officers to deter speeding, emphasizing the deterrent effect of severe penalties for speeding violations. Subsequently, hidden speeding cameras were installed on major roads to encourage cautious driving by creating uncertainty about when drivers were being monitored.

The latest approach in the ongoing battle against speeding involves placing a GPS device inside cars to incentivize drivers to maintain safe speeds. Researchers have discovered that a GPS device that monitors a vehicle's speed relative to the posted speed limit, coupled with a financial incentive, effectively reduces speeding behavior. In a study supported by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, drivers were offered a $25 reward each week for safe driving, with penalties deducted for exceeding speed limits.

The experiment demonstrated significant reductions in speeding violations, particularly for drivers exceeding speed limits by nine or more miles per hour. The combination of rewards for safe driving and penalties for speeding violations proved highly effective in modifying driver behavior. The study revealed that some drivers even turned the incentive system into a personal challenge, further motivating them to comply with speed limits.

The success of this incentive-based approach suggests potential applications beyond research studies. Ian Reagan, a traffic safety researcher, envisions insurance companies offering similar tracking devices to policyholders interested in reducing their premiums. Unlike current rebate programs, these devices would provide real-time feedback to drivers, informing them of the financial implications of their driving behavior after each trip.

In conclusion, this innovative method of using incentives to promote safe driving behavior represents a promising advancement in traffic safety initiatives. By combining rewards and penalties, authorities aim to encourage drivers to adhere to speed limits and reduce the risk of speeding-related accidents. The evolving landscape of traffic safety strategies may soon see widespread adoption of such incentive-based programs by insurance companies and other stakeholders.

Opioid use during pregnancy has risen dramatically, prompting new guidelines from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) aimed at improving care for affected women and newborns.  According to the CDC, 7% of U.S. women reported using prescription opioids during pregnancy in 2019, with one in five of those women misusing the drugs. By some estimates, nearly 80 infants born with opioid withdrawal are diagnosed daily in the U.S., a number that has tripled in recent years.

These infants can experience symptoms such as tremors, fussiness, and diarrhea, and may be at risk for developmental delays, though other factors like alcohol use, poor prenatal care, or stress could also contribute, according to Dr. Stephen Patrick, lead author of the AAP report.

The new guidelines, released Monday, address the critical need for consistent and effective care.  “While we have been talking about the opioid crisis for years, pregnant women and their newborns seldom make it to the top of the heap,” said Patrick, a Vanderbilt University pediatrician. “Infants are receiving variable care and not getting connected to services.”

The AAP recommends that pregnant women with opioid addiction have access to medication-assisted treatment.  Two opioids, buprenorphine and methadone, are effective, but pregnant women often face stigma when using them, and prescribing doctors are scarce.  Furthermore, hospitals should have written protocols for assessing and treating opioid-affected newborns, a practice currently lacking in many facilities.

The AAP also emphasizes the importance of breastfeeding and other bonding practices, along with parent education and referrals to support services for affected newborns. These recommendations echo guidance from other medical groups and the U.S. government.

The pandemic may be exacerbating the problem, making access to treatment even more difficult.  "Getting into treatment may be getting even harder," Patrick said.

# Populist Leaders Endanger Human Rights, Warns Advocacy Organization

*UNITED NATIONS, Jan 12, 2017 (IPS)* - Human Rights Watch warned that populist leaders pose a dangerous threat to human rights, fueling and justifying intolerance and abuse worldwide, during the launch of their annual global report.

In its 2017 World Report, titled "Demagogues Threaten Human Rights," the advocacy group emphasized the rise of populist leaders and their rhetoric that undermines the global human rights system as one of today's most pressing challenges.

"The rise of populism poses a profound threat to human rights," said Kenneth Roth, Human Rights Watch's Executive Director.

Roth explained that populist leaders, who claim to speak "for the people," treat rights as an "impediment" and scapegoat minority communities to address public discontent and domestic issues.

"Trump and various politicians in Europe seek power through appeals to racism, xenophobia, misogyny, and nativism. They all claim that the public accepts violations of human rights as supposedly necessary to secure jobs, avoid cultural change, or prevent terrorist attacks," he added.

The report highlights how President-elect Trump's campaign embodied this politics of intolerance, addressing Americans' economic frustrations and security fears by proposing controversial policies, including:
- Mass deportation of undocumented immigrants
- Creation of a Muslim registry
- Use of torture

If enacted, these proposals risk not only violating human rights but also undermining the entire human rights protection system.

European leaders have exhibited similar populist tendencies. The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination noted that the UK's Brexit campaign employed "divisive, anti-immigrant and xenophobic rhetoric," prompting calls for officials to reject such discourse.

Despite some progress in relocating asylum seekers, British Prime Minister Theresa May maintained an anti-rights stance, criticizing "activist left-wing human rights lawyers" and seeking to exempt UK forces abroad from human rights law.

Human Rights Watch emphasized that undermining rights for some threatens rights for all. "You may not like your neighbors, but if you sacrifice their rights today, you jeopardize your own tomorrow," Roth cautioned. "In fact, disregard for human rights offers the likeliest route to tyranny."

The rise of Western populism and muted response to violations has emboldened leaders worldwide:

- China's Xi Jinping has led an unprecedented crackdown on dissent
- Turkey's Erdoğan has crushed political and media opposition
- Burundi's Nkurunziza announced withdrawal from the International Criminal Court
- Syria's Assad and Saudi Arabia's Mohammad Bin Salman continue civilian attacks with apparent impunity

Akshaya Kumar, Human Rights Watch's Deputy UN Director, noted that populist leaders now embrace rather than shy away from anti-rights rhetoric. Examples include:

- Hungary's Viktor Orbán's open Islamophobia and anti-refugee policies
- Philippines' Rodrigo Duterte's explicit endorsement of extrajudicial killings

To combat these trends, Kumar advocates targeting enablers of rights abuses, including financial backers and arms suppliers. Recent successes include Canada's 2006 prohibition of LTTE fundraising and the U.S.'s 2016 suspension of arms sales to Philippine police.

The report emphasizes the crucial role of civil society organizations, media, and governments in defending human rights, particularly as some leaders "buried their heads in the sand, hoping the winds of populism will blow over."

Ultimately, the public bears responsibility for addressing populism and promoting human rights. As Roth concluded, "Values are fragile... A society's culture of respect for human rights needs regular tending, lest the fears of the moment sweep away the wisdom that built democratic rule."

Rainy Roth, a children’s ministry leader in her Montana church, volunteers as a crisis counselor with Crisis Text Line.  From her computer in a small town (population 943), she connects with people, primarily under 25, who are struggling with a variety of issues. This work, she finds, intertwines with her role at church, as both involve supporting and nurturing young people.

As a crisis counselor, Rainy completed a rigorous 34-hour training program, covering topics from active listening techniques to dealing with self-harm, suicide, depression, bullying, and gender/sexual identity.  This prepared her for the challenging but rewarding work ahead.

Rainy’s motivation stems partly from her own childhood experience with undiagnosed anxiety.  In the 1960s, mental health awareness was limited, and her struggles were misunderstood.  Now, she finds solace in being able to tell someone, “I get it,” offering understanding and validation she lacked as a child.

While she helps texters with various challenges, Rainy finds the “active rescues” – intervening when someone expresses imminent plans to harm themselves or others – particularly impactful.  Knowing she played a role in getting someone immediate help is profoundly rewarding. “It’s not only about saving lives,” she explains, “it’s also about letting these individuals know that people care.”

A simple phrase, “You matter,” carries surprising weight for many texters.  Rainy frequently hears, “Wow, I have never heard that before!”  These two words offer reassurance and a sense of belonging, countering negative thoughts and feelings.

The connection she forms with texters is deeply fulfilling.  Hearing them acknowledge her words brings a sense of comfort and, in a way, heals a part of herself that struggled for so long with unnamed fear and anxiety.  Being able to identify with their experiences allows her to help them understand that their feelings are valid and that there is hope for change.

Rainy believes she has become a better and healthier person through her work as a crisis counselor.  Her compassion, combined with the skills she gained through training, allows her to offer support and reassurance, letting those in crisis know that things will ultimately be okay.

The article "LeBron Delivers Cool Tribute to Steph as 3-Point Record Nears" was originally featured on NBC Sports Bay Area. As Steph Curry inches closer to breaking Ray Allen's record for the most 3-pointers in NBA history, his fellow players are reflecting on the remarkable legacy he has built since entering the NBA in 2009.

During a press conference on Friday night, LeBron James took a moment to praise Curry, using his iconic "we're all witnesses" phrase to emphasize Steph's brilliance. LeBron commended Steph, saying, "The fact that the other night we were really tracking to see if he would make 16 threes in a game, it just lets you know how freaking amazing this guy is. If there’s one guy in NBA history that can make 16 threes, it's Steph Curry."

LeBron went on to express his awe, stating, "I'm literally sitting there doing the calculations in my head. I'm like '16. OK, I know he's made 12 a few times. Well, if there's someone that can do it, it'll be him.' That just lets you know how incredible he is. You can't even jinx it, cause it's gonna happen. It may not happen tomorrow ... But it's going to happen. We're all witnesses to what Steph Curry has done in his career and the way that he's changed the game. He's a once-in-a-lifetime basketball player."

Steph and LeBron have emerged as two of the most prominent figures in the NBA, particularly following four consecutive years of meeting in the NBA Finals. As of Saturday night, Steph is only 10 3-pointers away from surpassing Allen's record of 2,973, with a game scheduled against the Philadelphia 76ers.

Once Curry breaks the record, we can expect an outpouring of sentiments similar to LeBron's heartfelt tribute. Even Allen himself has expressed his support for Steph, refraining from heckling him as he approaches the milestone and offering guidance throughout the process.

Allen shared, "It's an exciting time for him and I tried to give him what I was dealing with, you know, going into the game and everything that led up to it. And I was fortunate because I broke the record in Boston against the [Los Angeles] Lakers with Reggie in the building, so it's only appropriate that I find my way there. I don't know where it's going to be so I got to kind of watch this thing."

Should Curry not break the record on Saturday, his next opportunity will come on Monday against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis. The Warriors are reportedly contemplating resting Steph for that game, depending on the outcome of the Saturday match in Philadelphia.

# Athens Olympics: A Decade Later - Promise, Pride, and Missed Opportunities

## The Dream Begins
After failing in a bid to host the centennial Olympics in 1996, Greece, founder of the ancient and modern Olympics, was awarded the 2004 Games after defeating favorites Rome. The announcement sparked jubilant celebrations, with the Greek delegation, including then-minister George Papandreou, erupting in joy. The moment was so significant that a DJ-remixed version of the announcement was even released as a single.

## From Euphoria to Reality
However, the initial euphoria quickly gave way to challenges. Athens wasted the first three years of its seven-year preparation period, prompting a warning from the IOC in 2000 to accelerate its efforts or risk losing the Games. This led to a frenzied construction period, with crews working three shifts daily to complete venues just weeks before the opening ceremony.

The Games ultimately cost Greece an estimated $11 billion—double the initial projections. New infrastructure emerged across Athens: trams, highways, and gleaming Olympic venues appeared alongside the city's existing architecture. Banners proudly proclaimed "Welcome Home" during the Games.

## A Decade of Decay
Today, ten years later, the legacy of the 2004 Olympics tells a different story:

- The once-gleaming Olympic venues now largely stand abandoned
- The former canoe and kayak venue has dried up, with spectator seats torn out
- At the Olympic rowing center in Marathon, stray dogs roam among overgrown weeds
- Many venues are used only occasionally for non-sporting events like conferences and weddings

## The Economic Impact
For Greeks who once swelled with pride, the Games have become a source of frustration as the country struggles through:
- A six-year depression
- Record unemployment
- Rising homelessness and poverty

While the Hellenic Olympic Committee maintains that the Games' €8.5 billion cost didn't significantly contribute to Greece's €360 billion debt crisis, critics argue differently.

Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand is visiting Long Island Friday to discuss new bipartisan legislation that would expand the U.S. Small Business Administration’s microloan program. Gillibrand was making a stop at Farmingdale State College to say that the Mircoloan Modernization Act would make it easier for entrepreneurs to access capital to grow their business. The new legislation would be of benefit to women and minority business owners, along with other entrepreneurs, who struggle with access to capital because banks often deny them loans to start and grow a business.

Gillibrand said the act would raise the total limit on outstanding loans to intermediary lending organizations, allowing for more loans to be made to women, minority and other business owners. It would also expand the number of opportunities for more hands-on training assistance so that more small business owners can succeed. Women receive less than 5 percent of conventional small business loans, yet they own nearly 40 percent of businesses across the nation, according to the U.S. Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship. And loan denial rates for minority firms were nearly three times higher than those of non-minority-owned firms, U.S. Department of Commerce reports.

This bipartisan legislation was sponsored by Sen. Deb Fischer (R-NE) and has passed in the House of Representatives. The bill is also cosponsored by Senators Tim Scott (R-SC), Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Joe Donnelly (D-IN), and Gary Peters (D-MI).

Laois Kayak & Canoe Club members Brian Ogilvie, Finbar O’Donovan, and Jim Tierney paddled their way to a historic gold medal at the 2018 Liffey Descent. This victory marks the first Liffey Descent gold for any Laois club.  The Canadian Triple class team faced challenging conditions in the grueling 32km race, which started at the K Club in Straffan, Co Kildare.

Over 500 kayakers from around the world competed in this year's event, made more technical by low water levels resulting from a summer drought and the lack of an upstream flood release by the ESB.  The challenging course included 11 weirs and one portage, making the race particularly tough.  The trio finished with a winning time of 3 hours 50 minutes, acknowledging it was the toughest race they had ever paddled, making the victory even sweeter.

“The key to the race was getting a strong start and reading the river correctly,” Finbar O’Donovan told the Leinster Express. “We knew that it would spell disaster if we took the wrong route over the high drops. Luckily, we got everything right on the day.”  The less experienced competitors faced carnage on the big weirs, highlighting the skill and precision required to navigate the challenging course.

Congratulations are also extended to Laois Kayak & Canoe Club members Seamus Byrne, Matt McGrath, Patrick Marshall, and Catherine Byrne, who all finished the race with commendable times.

# Wall Street Growing Cautious on FANG Stocks

Wall Street is getting jittery over FANG stocks, with particular concern focused on tech giant Alphabet. FANG—an acronym created by CNBC's Jim Cramer—represents a basket of high-growth technology stocks: Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Alphabet (formerly known as Google).

Despite FANG stocks significantly outperforming the market this year—Facebook up 31%, Amazon up 30%, Netflix up 23%, and Alphabet up 22%, compared to the S&P 500's 9% return—analysts are beginning to express valuation concerns.

In a note to clients Thursday, Canaccord Genuity analyst Michael Graham downgraded Alphabet to "hold" from "buy," while maintaining his $1,000 price target, which represents just 3% upside from Wednesday's close. The stock, which recently reached the $1,000 level for the first time, is down 2% in Thursday premarket trading following the report.

Graham outlined three key reasons for the downgrade:

1. Limited growth potential: "We think much of the growth over the past two years is due to ad load increases on mobile search and YouTube, which (especially the former) will be hard to repeat."

2. Margin pressure: "Our refreshed detailed segment analysis suggests firmly that consensus gross margin estimates are too high, and while revenue growth mostly makes up for this, we believe this limits the potential for upward EPS revisions."

3. Valuation concerns: "GOOGL's P/E multiple of ~24x is expensive by historical standards, and puts the stock within a pitching wedge of our $1,000 price target."

## Stuffed Oats Chilla
A health-conscious twist on traditional chilla, made with oat flour and vegetable stuffing. Perfect for breakfast, a wholesome snack, or main course.

### Ingredients
For the Chilla:
- 1 cup oats (powdered)
- 2 tbsp gram flour (besan)
- 1½ tsp oil
- ½ tsp chopped green chilies
- 1 cup water
- ½ tsp turmeric powder (haldi)
- ½ tsp asafetida (hing)
- 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves
- Salt to taste
- 3 tsp oil for cooking

For the Vegetable Stuffing:
- ½ cup boiled green peas
- ½ cup boiled potatoes, peeled & chopped
- ½ tbsp oil
- 1 tbsp chopped onions
- 1 tbsp chopped tomatoes
- ½ tsp turmeric powder
- ½ tsp garam masala
- Pinch of asafetida
- Salt and chili powder to taste
- 1 cup tamarind chutney for serving

### Method
1. **For the Stuffing:**
   - Heat oil in a vessel
   - Add turmeric powder, garam masala, asafetida, onions, and tomatoes; sauté for 30 seconds
   - Add green peas, potatoes, salt, and chili powder; cook for 2 minutes

2. **For the Chilla:**
   - Combine gram flour, green chilies, asafetida, coriander, turmeric powder, powdered oats, oil, water, and salt
   - Heat oil in a non-stick pan
   - Pour batter and spread into a round shape
   - Cook both sides until done
   - Add stuffing, fold, and serve hot with tamarind chutney

Rents in London have decreased during the Coronavirus pandemic, according to property portal Zoopla. However, London remains an exception, as rents have risen in a vibrant rental market across the UK as a whole.

"Average rents in London have fallen by 5.2 percent over the last 12 months, reaching levels last seen in 2014," Zoopla reported. This decline is attributed to "new working patterns and the lack of tourism during the pandemic."

In contrast, rents outside of London increased by 1.7 percent, and rental demand has surged by a fifth over the past year. This strong demand is driven by a squeeze on lending to potential first-time buyers, Zoopla explained. 

"At the same time, supply remains constrained, with investment in buy-to-let properties still reduced following changes to Stamp Duty (the additional 3 percent surcharge on second properties) and the broader tax regime introduced from 2016 onwards."

Renters are increasingly interested in larger properties, particularly those with access to outdoor spaces. 

"The search for space, first observed in the sales market, is now being strongly replicated by renters. Zoopla's top searches for rental properties include terms like gardens, parking, garages, balconies, and pets, reflecting a need for outdoor space and freedom necessary to cope with lockdown. There is also evidence that while the market as a whole is moving more quickly, the market for rented houses is moving more rapidly than that for rented flats, highlighting this desire for more space among renters."

"For most of the UK, the demand-supply gap is supporting moderate levels of rental growth," said Zoopla's head of research, Gráinne Gilmore.

"The split in the rental market caused by COVID-19 has now become pronounced, and we are witnessing a firmly entrenched two-speed market. 

"We haven't seen an exodus of students from cities, and as more people remain in the rental market due to the squeeze on mortgage lending, higher levels of demand will continue to support rents. However, muted earnings growth will begin to limit the potential for rental growth in some markets. 

"The search for additional space, both indoor and outdoor, within the rental sector is set to continue as the country experiences further lockdown periods."

ETH Zurich, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, is a leading institution known for its focus on science and technology. Established in 1855, it has become a center of innovation, channeling research into high-tech sectors like computer science, micro and nanotechnology, and medicine. The university boasts an impressive track record, with 21 Nobel laureates having studied, taught, or researched there. ETH Zurich has established its presence beyond Switzerland through initiatives like the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC).

In 2010, Dr. Remo Burkhard moved to Singapore to build the Singapore-ETH Centre, the first research center established by ETH Zurich outside Switzerland. The center was established in collaboration with the National Research Foundation of Singapore under its Campus for Research Excellence and Technological Enterprise (CREATE) program. It aims to tackle pressing urban challenges in collaboration with Singaporean universities, government agencies, and industry.

Since its founding, the Singapore-ETH Centre has become a vibrant research hub with approximately 200 researchers working under two main programs: Future Cities Laboratory (FCL) and Future Resilient Systems (FRS). FCL, established in 2010, focuses on making cities more sustainable and livable, while FRS, launched in 2014, aims to enhance the resilience of infrastructure systems.

A pioneering project under the Future Cities Laboratory is the Cooling Singapore initiative. Led by SEC director Gerhard Schmitt, the project seeks to mitigate the urban heat island (UHI) effect in Singapore and improve outdoor thermal comfort (OTC) and liveability. The initiative aligns with Singapore's commitment to reduce emission intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030.

"As urban centers like Singapore become more densely populated, more heat is generated, impacting the environment. The Cooling Singapore project aims to address these challenges," says Dr. Burkhard. The project received a grant from Singapore's National Research Foundation in 2017, bringing together expertise from the National University of Singapore (NUS), SMART (Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology), and TUMCREATE.

The Cooling Singapore project has a multifaceted approach. It seeks to establish an inter-agency task force comprising members from various Singaporean agencies and institutions to exchange knowledge through workshops. This collaboration is crucial as tackling UHI involves economic development, urban planning, and transportation, requiring the collective effort of scientists, agencies, industry, and policymakers.

One of the project's key tasks is applying microscale climate models to study areas like Jurong Lake District, the Central Business District, and Punggol. These case studies help researchers understand how OTC varies and how different urban designs can mitigate UHI. Initial results suggest a need for more scientific research, pointing towards improving efficiency and cost-effectiveness in strategy implementation.

Beyond policy and planning, businesses and individuals also play a role in mitigating urban heating. "Heat is trapped and released from roads and buildings; energy consumption in industry and transportation are significant contributors to UHI," explains Dr. Burkhard. **GREEN BAY, Wis. —** Dale Cihlar, typically a buoyant and optimistic farmer, found himself in despair. Several of his prized dairy cows had died, milk prices were plummeting, and he faced a $1,600 monthly payment for a new manure storage system.

"I've never been in debt like this," said Dale, a fourth-generation dairy farmer who took over the family farm in 1990. He and his wife, Karen, sat at their kitchen table, surrounded by a mound of paperwork—some detailing milk prices, others highlighting their income struggles.

After unsuccessful appeals to various banks, Dale considered selling part of the farm to make ends meet. However, Karen had a different plan, one she hadn't shared with her husband.

"He's too proud, but I thought if people knew, maybe they would help," she told USA Today Network-Wisconsin.

Karen took to GoFundMe, a crowdfunding platform, to write a heartfelt plea to save the family farm. Her adult children and their friends shared the campaign on Facebook, and donations began to trickle in. As word spread on social media, Karen received calls from local farmers offering help, including one who had extra hay.

The community, including friends, family, and strangers, rallied to prevent the demise of another family farm. Donations poured in from people in other states as well.

Since 1873, the Cihlar family has farmed the 110-acre property, sustaining the family for generations. To handle the historical fluctuations in milk prices, Dale had embraced the budgeting practices of his forebears, saving diligently to cover large expenses and ride out price swings.

Frugality was so ingrained in Dale's psyche that he didn't marry Karen until he made his last payment on the family farm. Although milk prices had been low before, they had never been this low for three consecutive years.

Savings among dairy farmers were depleting across the state. Wisconsin lost 500 dairy farms in 2017, and more than 150 had quit milking cows so far this year. The number of milk herds dropped by 20% from five years ago, according to the state Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection.

The Cihlar farm weathered these highs and lows until a perfect storm of issues hit. The historically low milk checks worsened after several prized cows died, and the $1,600 monthly manure storage system payment drained the farm’s savings.

Dale and Karen managed to squeak by on Karen’s salary from the Door County Medical Center, but their savings were exhausted. For over 100 years, the 110-acre farm and 40 cows had supported the Cihlar family.

"I couldn't be the last one. I've always thought this farm would last and be part of my family far into the future," Dale said.

In less than a month, the GoFundMe page Karen created raised enough money to buy one cow. After a month, they'd raised nearly $8,000 of the $35,000 goal.

"I started to cry. I couldn't believe that people were actually helping us," Karen said.

When Karen showed Dale the GoFundMe site and the donations, he was dumbfounded.

"There are so many causes needing help, and I thought no one would ever want to help a farmer," Dale said, shaking his head. "I was wrong; this is beyond words."

The cost of a dairy cow ranges from $1,000 to $1,600, with significant additional expenses for feed and veterinary care.

While the financial support was crucial, the campaign had a broader impact by highlighting the plight of dairy farmers and showing that people can help. Offers of free feed poured in, and farmers leaving the business sold some stock to the Cihlars at reduced rates to ensure the farm's success.

Dale's extended family also pitched in to keep the farm within the family.

"I'm the only cousin still in farming, and this farm means a lot to them too," he said.

Besides the donations, Dale took a part-time truck-driving job to help make ends meet. Despite knowing firsthand the challenges of dairy farming, both Dale's stepson and son-in-law are determined to keep the farm in the family. They plan to take over when Dale retires, assisting with farm chores while maintaining their day jobs.

"They help out every morning and night and know it's not easy," Dale said.

Ethan Lautenbach, Karen's son from her first marriage, shares Dale's passion for farming.

"It's a challenge every day," Ethan said, adding that he enjoys the lifestyle.

Son-in-law Steven Baxter grew up on a small goat farm in Texas and is president of the Door County Farm Bureau. Like Dale, Steven is captivated by the animals and sees them as integral to the business.

"If it wasn't for their milk, we wouldn't have a dairy," Steven said. "When a calf is born, it's a miracle, and we do everything to ensure it grows up healthy because, in the long run, that cow is what takes care of us."

# Internet Governance Conference Shifts Focus as US Signals Change

A global conference on Internet governance in Brazil is expected to be less contentious than initially anticipated, following the United States' willingness to relax its control over key Internet functions.

The US has agreed to relinquish oversight of the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) - a California-based nonprofit responsible for managing domain names - responding to demands from Brazil and other nations following revelations of widespread electronic surveillance.

"The focus has shifted from a political reaction to the NSA allegations toward more constructive criticism and dialogue about the Internet's future," notes William Beer, a São Paulo-based cybersecurity expert.

The Net Mundial conference, a two-day event in São Paulo opening Wednesday under Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff, will address several crucial topics:

- Cybersecurity
- Privacy protection
- Freedom of expression
- Future oversight of the decentralized network

Representatives from diverse nations - including China, Cuba, the United States, and European countries - will participate. However, organizers emphasize that government officials will share equal standing with:

- Internet companies
- Academic institutions
- Technical experts
- Internet user advocacy groups

"All stakeholders deserve equal participation in this multi-stakeholder process," explains Virgilio Almeida, Brazil's IT policy secretary and conference chair.

While the conference isn't expected to produce binding decisions, Almeida suggests it will initiate an important dialogue that will "sow the seeds" for future Internet governance reforms.

## Background and Context

The conference emerges from controversy surrounding NSA surveillance programs, which targeted multiple world leaders, including:

- Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff
- German Chancellor Angela Merkel

These revelations, disclosed by former NSA analyst Edward Snowden, prompted international calls to reduce US control over the Internet - a network originally created 50 years ago to connect American universities with the defense industry.

## ICANN Transition

In a surprising move last month, the US government announced plans to transfer ICANN oversight to an international body by September 2015. This transition comes with one crucial condition: the new organization cannot be under any government's control.

The debate over ICANN's future management likely represents a new point of contention, particularly with nations advocating for multilateral control through organizations like the United Nations.

China, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan have jointly proposed developing a UN-based Internet code of conduct. However, this proposal - originating from countries known for Internet censorship - is unlikely to gain widespread support at the conference.

"Most participants here favor a multi-stakeholder model for the Internet," Almeida told Reuters. "China prefers a UN treaty approach, but the UN only represents governments."

After running a mobile food business for the past five years, a woman from Etna is gearing up to introduce her authentic Jamaican cuisine to a storefront at the Shoppes at Turnberry in early 2022.

However, her passion for cooking the traditional dishes of her parents' homeland, such as jerk-style cuisine, overshadowed her journalistic ambitions. Jerk-style involves dry-rubbing or wet marinating meat with a flavorful and spicy mixture.

Honoring her heritage, Jackson discovered her love for preparing meals not only for herself but also for larger groups of people. "I realized that others enjoyed my food, and I had a strong desire to cook for a wider audience," expressed Jackson.

In 2016, she took the leap to convert her passion into a profession by launching Twinado Kitchen's Jerk Shack, a mobile food business that she initially operated from tents at festivals and pop-up events. The business, named after her twin sons, aged 8, quickly gained popularity. In 2017, she upgraded to a trailer to expand her services further.

Looking towards the future, Jackson aims to establish a permanent presence at The Shoppes at Turnberry in January or February, underscoring the need for a larger space as demand for her cuisine continues to surge. "We have truly outgrown the trailer," Jackson stated. "Our customer base is growing, especially from Pickerington, and I see the potential with the area's expansion."

The exact address of the upcoming establishment is pending as the space is undergoing conversion from a storage unit located between Omezzo Restaurant & Pizzeria at 1755 Hill Road North and Goodwill at 1771 Hill Road North.

Upon opening, the 39-year-old entrepreneur plans to operate the eatery for carryout exclusively from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Saturday, offering an array of dishes including jerk chicken, jerk beef, various jerk seafood options, oxtail, and lamb chops. Jackson's anticipation is mirrored by city officials, who are thrilled that she has chosen Pickerington for her storefront venture.

On Monday, Dec. 13, a judge in Rochester Hills, Mich., declined the request to move 15-year-old Ethan Crumbley, charged with killing four students and injuring others in a shooting at Oxford High School, out of an adult jail. Crumbley is charged as an adult with killing four classmates and injuring seven other people in the Nov. 30 shooting at Oxford High School, about 30 miles (50 kilometers) north of Detroit.

During his probable cause conference, Crumbley’s attorney, Paulette Loftin, argued that he should be moved back to a juvenile facility, stating that he "should not be considered a menace to other juveniles." Loftin emphasized that Crumbley had no prior history of trouble and that the incident was isolated.

Assistant Oakland County Prosecutor Marc Keast countered Loftin's argument, highlighting the severity of the charges and security concerns as reasons for Crumbley to remain in an adult facility. Keast emphasized that the shooting was not an isolated incident but a planned, premeditated mass murder targeting juveniles.

Judge Nancy Carniak sided with Keast and ruled that Crumbley would remain in the adult jail. She adjourned the probable cause hearing to Jan. 7 to review witness statements and evidence. A competency exam may be ordered at a later date if requested by Crumbley's attorneys.

The school officials met with Ethan Crumbley and his parents on the morning of the shooting after a concerning drawing was found. Despite this, the Crumbleys refused to take their son home. James Crumbley had purchased the gun used in the shooting just days before, and their son had access to it.

Crumbley's parents, James and Jennifer Crumbley, are also being held at the jail and face charges of involuntary manslaughter for failing to intervene on the day of the tragedy. Their hearings are scheduled for the following day, Tuesday.

The conference on Monday was a procedural hearing to prepare for a preliminary hearing set for Dec. 20, which will be rescheduled. Keast assured that steps would be taken to ensure Crumbley is separated from adult inmates at the jail to protect his safety.

Overall, the court proceedings and decisions surrounding Crumbley's case reflect the gravity of the charges and the complexities involved in addressing such a tragic event.

SHREVEPORT, La. (KTAL/KMSS) – The Caddo Parish Sheriff’s Office has introduced a new facility dedicated to housing loose livestock collected by their team. This two-acre holding pen, located behind the Caddo Correctional Center, is designed to accommodate horses, cows, goats, domestic pigs, and donkeys that frequently escape from pastures and other enclosures within the parish.

The Sheriff’s Office Stock Patrol retrieves loose livestock on a weekly—and sometimes daily—basis. Some animals remain for just a few hours until their owners are found, while others may stay for several weeks. The new facility features three covered holding areas, a gated unloading zone, and a barn equipped with two stalls. It was constructed by the Sheriff's Office's Building and Grounds and Livestock Patrol teams.

The total cost of building the holding pen was approximately $17,000, which includes donations and in-kind services.

The upcoming super-middleweight title clash between Chris Eubank Jr. and George Groves promises to be a 2018 highlight, a potential 12-round classic.  Beyond the excitement of Eubank Jr.’s inherited self-belief and blinding hand speed, this fight represents a pivotal moment in the younger Eubank’s career.  As Dr. Samuel Johnson, the great man of letters, wrote nearly 300 years ago: “There must always be a struggle between father and son, while one aims at power and the other at independence.” This struggle is embodied in the Eubanks.

Chris Eubank Sr., a former illustrious double world champion, has been a constant, arguably overbearing, presence in his son’s career.  Much like a Svengali, he has dominated and monitored almost every move his son has made, both inside and outside the ring.  This fight offers Eubank Jr., at 28, the chance to step out of his father's shadow and forge his own identity. He acknowledges this, stating his desire to be recognized as Chris Eubank, not simply Chris Eubank Jr.  A victory over Groves would be a significant step in that direction.

While Eubank Jr. enters the fight as a surprising favorite, endorsed by a 20-10 margin in a Boxing Monthly poll of British professionals, Groves, the reigning WBA super-middleweight champion, presents a formidable challenge.  Groves, making his third title defense, will need his sharp jab and honed defensive skills to weather the early-round onslaught expected from Eubank Jr.  Although Eubank Jr. boasts impressive speed and confidence, his opponents, with the exception of Billy Joe Saunders (who defeated him on points), haven't been of the same caliber as those Groves has faced.

I question Eubank Jr.'s power at this weight.  He might have been better suited staying at middleweight. I doubt he possesses the power to seriously trouble the top super-middleweights.  While Groves has suffered two losses to Carl Froch, including a brutal knockout in their second bout, his size advantage in this fight could be decisive.

Contrary to popular opinion, I believe Groves’s counter-punching and precise timing will carry him to a close but clear points victory.  His size and experience against top-tier competition will ultimately prove too much for Eubank Jr. to overcome.  This fight isn't just about a title; it's about a son's fight for independence and recognition in his own right.

# Finland Approves €8.5M Artillery Ammunition Sale to Estonia

The Finnish government has approved a proposal to supply ammunition for Estonia's 155mm howitzer artillery systems, as confirmed by the Finnish Defence Ministry on Friday. The deal, valued at €8.5 million (excluding taxes), marks another step in strengthening defense cooperation between the two nations.

The formal agreement for the artillery rounds will be finalized through a signing ceremony between both countries' defense ministries in the coming weeks. At the Estonian government's request, specific details regarding ammunition quantity and specifications will remain classified.

The ammunition will be sourced from Finland's existing stockpiles, with the Defense Ministry emphasizing that this transaction won't compromise Finland's own defense capabilities. Finnish defense contractor Nammo Lapua Oy manufactured the majority of the ammunition.

This agreement builds upon ongoing artillery-focused collaboration between the two nations. It follows Estonia's recent decision to acquire South Korean K9 Thunder self-propelled howitzers—the same system Finland chose to procure in early 2017.
